description: Add scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs: a committed, dependency-free Node script that keeps the five ARG <TOOL>_SHA256 values in the Dockerfile in sync with the five ARG <TOOL>_VERSION values. For each tool it resolves the checksum published upstream, independently downloads the artifact and recomputes its SHA-256, and refuses to emit a value unless the two agree. That two-source agreement is what preserves audit finding S-01: the checksum committed in the repo remains an independently attested expectation rather than something trusted blindly at build time. The script has a --write mode (rewrite the ARG lines) and a --check mode (exit non-zero on mismatch, for CI). This feature delivers and proves the script only; wiring it into Renovate and CI is FEAT-003.
steps: Create scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs, executable (chmod +x) with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang. Use Node ESM and the standard library ONLY: node:fs, node:crypto, node:process, and global fetch. Do NOT add a package.json, node_modules, or any npm dependency, and do NOT shell out to curl or jq. Reason: the script must run inside the ghcr.io/renovatebot/renovate container in FEAT-003, which ships Node but does not guarantee curl or jq.

Define a table of the five tools keyed by the Dockerfile ARG prefix (GWS, GH, KUBECTL, DEVIN, GO). For each entry record: the artifact URL template, the upstream-checksum resolution strategy, and a human-readable tool name. Use exactly the sources verified in context.json key_patterns. gws: artifact https://github.com/googleworkspace/cli/releases/download/v${V}/google-workspace-cli-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz, checksum from the same URL with '.sha256' appended, format '<hex>  <filename>' so take the first whitespace-separated field. gh: artifact https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/download/v${V}/gh_${V}_linux_amd64.tar.gz, checksum from https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/download/v${V}/gh_${V}_checksums.txt, select the line whose filename field is exactly gh_${V}_linux_amd64.tar.gz (do not substring-match, the file also lists .deb and .rpm artifacts). kubectl: artifact https://dl.k8s.io/release/v${V}/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl (a raw binary, not a tarball), checksum from that URL with '.sha256' appended, bare hex with no filename field. devin: artifact https://static.devin.ai/cli/${V}/devin-${V}-x86_64-unknown-linux.tar.gz, checksum from https://static.devin.ai/cli/${V}/manifest.json at .platforms['x86_64-unknown-linux'].sha256 (the per-version manifest exists, do not use /cli/current/manifest.json which always returns the newest version). go: artifact https://go.dev/dl/go${V}.linux-amd64.tar.gz, checksum from https://go.dev/dl/?mode=json&include=all by selecting the entry whose .version equals `go${V}` then the file with os==='linux', arch==='amd64', kind==='archive', field .sha256.

CRITICAL: do not implement the Go checksum by fetching https://go.dev/dl/go${V}.linux-amd64.tar.gz.sha256. That URL returns an HTML error page with HTTP 200-style rendering, not a hash. This was verified by execution. Every checksum fetch must validate that the extracted value matches /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/ and fail loudly with the URL and the first 200 characters of the response body if it does not, so this class of mistake can never silently produce a garbage ARG value.

Parse the Dockerfile by reading it as text and matching, per tool prefix, `ARG <PREFIX>_VERSION=<value>` and `ARG <PREFIX>_SHA256=<hex>`. Fail with a clear error if either line is missing for any of the five prefixes, so a future Dockerfile refactor cannot make the script silently skip a tool.

For each selected tool: fetch the upstream published checksum, then download the artifact and compute its SHA-256 by streaming through node:crypto createHash (do not buffer the whole 300 MB Go tarball in memory; pipe the response body into the hash). Compare the two. If they differ, abort the whole run with a non-zero exit and a message naming the tool, the version, the artifact URL, the upstream-published value and the computed value. Never write a value that failed this cross-check.

Implement the CLI: `--write` rewrites the ARG <PREFIX>_SHA256 line in place, touching only that one line per tool and leaving every other byte of the Dockerfile unchanged (no reformatting, no trailing-newline change, no reordering of the layer blocks, which are deliberately ordered per P-02). `--check` (the default when no mode flag is given) writes nothing and exits 1 if any committed value differs from the verified upstream value, printing a diff-style line per mismatch. `--only=<name>` restricts the run to one tool, accepting the lowercase tool name (gws, gh, kubectl, devin, go) and being tolerant of the Renovate depName spellings that will be passed in FEAT-003, namely googleworkspace/cli, cli/cli, kubernetes/kubernetes, devin-cli and golang; an unrecognised value must exit 0 without writing anything and print that it matched no managed tool, so a Renovate upgrade for an unrelated dependency such as an Action or the base image cannot fail the task. `--help` prints usage.
Print a concise per-tool status line in both modes (tool, version, OK or MISMATCH, and in --write mode whether the file was changed) and a summary line, so the CI log in FEAT-003 is readable.

Add a short header comment in the script explaining why it exists (Renovate cannot resolve a tarball SHA-256 as a digest for these datasources), why it cross-checks two sources (S-01), and that it must remain dependency-free.

PROOF 1 (no-op on a correct tree): run `node scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs --check` against the unmodified Dockerfile. All five tools must report OK and the exit code must be 0. Then run `node scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs --write` and confirm `git diff -- Dockerfile` is empty, proving the script is idempotent and does not churn the file.

PROOF 2 (reproduces the PR #26 fix): edit the Dockerfile to `ARG GO_VERSION=1.27.1` (exactly the change on branch origin/renovate/golang-1.x), leaving GO_SHA256 stale. Run `node scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs --check` and confirm it exits non-zero and names GO as the mismatch. Then run `node scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs --write --only=golang` and assert GO_SHA256 is now exactly 63d339f0da5ab53635a56f2490a7984dfe12dfcff22ad749f63edaf590168445, and that `git diff -- Dockerfile` shows exactly two changed lines (GO_VERSION and GO_SHA256) and no change to the other four SHA256 ARGs.

PROOF 3 (the image actually builds): with the simulated 1.27.1 + corrected checksum state in place, run `docker build -t hermes-leo-custom:go1271 .` and confirm it exits 0, then run the five smoke commands from pr-validation.yml against that tag and confirm `--entrypoint go ... version` reports go1.27.1, and re-check entrypoint and architecture. This is the end-state proof that PR #26 would go green.

PROOF 4 (failure path is real): temporarily corrupt one committed checksum (for example flip a character in GWS_SHA256), run `--check`, confirm it exits non-zero and names GWS, then restore. This proves --check is not vacuously passing.

Revert the Dockerfile to the committed main state (GO_VERSION=1.27.0 with its matching checksum) so this branch does not carry the Go bump itself: the point of the change is the mechanism, and Renovate will re-propose the bump. Confirm with `git diff -- Dockerfile` being empty.
Record in the feature's `findings` field: the exact output of each of the four proofs, the go1.27.1 checksum produced, and the go version reported by the built image.

Commit with a Conventional Commits message, for example `feat(scripts): synchroniser les SHA-256 des 5 téléchargements depuis les sources upstream`. Commit scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs and the .agents/ state; the Dockerfile must NOT appear in the diff.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs exists, is executable, has a node shebang, imports only node: built-ins and uses global fetch, and the repo still contains no package.json and no node_modules.
`node scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs --check` exits 0 on the unmodified Dockerfile and prints OK for all five tools.
`node scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs --write` on the unmodified Dockerfile leaves `git diff -- Dockerfile` empty.

With ARG GO_VERSION=1.27.1, `--check` exits non-zero and names GO, and `--write --only=golang` sets GO_SHA256 to exactly 63d339f0da5ab53635a56f2490a7984dfe12dfcff22ad749f63edaf590168445 while changing no other SHA256 ARG.
`docker build` of that simulated state exits 0 and `docker run --rm --entrypoint go version` reports go1.27.1.
Corrupting a committed checksum makes `--check` exit non-zero and name the affected tool.
A checksum fetch that does not yield 64 hex characters causes a loud failure naming the URL, rather than writing the response body into the Dockerfile.
`--only=` with an unmanaged value exits 0 and writes nothing.
The final committed Dockerfile is byte-identical to main (still GO_VERSION=1.27.0).
All four proofs and their outputs are recorded in the feature's findings field.
verification: sed -i 's/^ARG GO_VERSION=1.27.0$/ARG GO_VERSION=1.27.1/' Dockerfile && node scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs --check ; echo "expected non-zero, got $?"

node scripts/sync-download-checksums.mjs --write --only=golang && grep -n '^ARG GO_SHA256=63d339f0da5ab53635a56f2490a7984dfe12dfcff22ad749f63edaf590168445$' Dockerfile && git diff --stat -- Dockerfile

docker build -t hermes-leo-custom:go1271 . && docker run --rm --entrypoint go hermes-leo-custom:go1271 version && docker run --rm --entrypoint gws hermes-leo-custom:go1271 --version && docker run --rm --entrypoint gh hermes-leo-custom:go1271 --version && docker run --rm --entrypoint kubectl hermes-leo-custom:go1271 version --client && docker run --rm --entrypoint devin hermes-leo-custom:go1271 --version
docker image inspect hermes-leo-custom:go1271 --format '{{json .Config.Entrypoint}}' && docker image inspect hermes-leo-custom:go1271 --format '{{.Architecture}}'
git checkout -- Dockerfile && git diff --exit-code -- Dockerfile
